response: Yes, common carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) can serve as an indicator of both cardiovascular phenotype and risk among black Africans. CIMT is a non-invasive measure of the thickness of the intimal and medial layers of the carotid artery and is widely recognized as a surrogate marker for atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease. Studies have shown that increased CIMT is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events, such as heart attacks and strokes, in various populations, including black Africans. Therefore, CIMT can be a useful tool for assessing cardiovascular risk and phenotype in this population.
